 * ServiceNow Development: Design, develop, and implement ServiceNow applications, modules, and integrations using best practices and industry standards. 

 * Customization and Configuration: Customize and configure ServiceNow modules and workflows to meet specific business requirements and improve overall system functionality. 

 * Application Design: Collaborate with stakeholders to gather and analyze business needs and translate them into functional requirements and technical specifications for ServiceNow applications. 

 * Integration Development: Develop and maintain integrations between ServiceNow and other external systems, applications, and databases, ensuring seamless data flow and system interoperability. 

 * Automation and Scripting: Utilize scripting languages such as JavaScript and ServiceNow-specific scripting tools to automate tasks, create business rules, and enhance system functionalities. 

 * Technical Support: Provide technical support and troubleshooting assistance to users, addressing issues related to ServiceNow applications, configurations, and integrations. 

 * Testing and Quality Assurance: Conduct thorough testing and debugging of ServiceNow applications to ensure accuracy, performance, and reliability, identifying and resolving any defects or issues. 

 * Documentation: Create detailed technical documentation, including system designs, configuration guides, and user manuals, to facilitate effective system maintenance, support, and knowledge transfer. 

 * Collaboration and Communication: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including implementation partners, business analysts, system administrators, project managers, and the Manager, ServiceNow Centre of Excellence to ensure successful project delivery and timely resolution of issues. 

 * Teamwork: Participate in group and peer code review sessions for quality assurance and adherence to standardized practices. 

 * Release Management: Support application rollout and upgrade projects by working with our internal teams as well as vendors. Prioritize tasks and provide status updates.  This may involve non-business hour work. 

 * Attend requirement gathering sessions with business units to clarify the required behaviour, and the risks and impacts to the Bank. 

 * Support the Manager, ServiceNow Centre of Excellence with status report generation and backlog prioritization. 

## Let's Talk About You!

 * Education: bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent experience. 

 * Experience: Minimum of 2 years of experience as a ServiceNow Developer or a similar role, working with ServiceNow platform and related technologies. 

 * ServiceNow Expertise: In-depth knowledge and hands-on experience with ServiceNow platform, modules, and development tools, including ServiceNow application development tools, workflows, UI policies, business rules, and client scripts. 

 * Technical Skills: Proficient in JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and other web technologies. Experience with REST and SOAP web services, XML, JSON, and database concepts. 

 * ServiceNow Certifications: Preferred certifications include Certified Application Developer (CAD), Certified Implementation Specialist (CIS), or other relevant ServiceNow certifications. 

 * Problem-Solving Abilities: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to understand complex business requirements and translate them into effective technical solutions. 

 * Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams and articulate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. 

 * Team Player: Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment, contributing to a positive and supportive work culture. 

 * Attention to Detail: Strong attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality work with a focus on accuracy and precision. 

 * Adaptability: Flexibility to adapt to changing priorities and project requirements, demonstrating a proactive and results-oriented approach. 

 * Continuous Learning: Eagerness to stay up to date with the latest ServiceNow developments, technologies, and industry trends, and willingness to continuously expand and refine technical skills.

jobs.title: Senior People Partner
jobs.description_text:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.




ABOUT THE ROLE

KOHO is in the middle of a meaningful shift - from a traditional P&C function to a modern People Enablement model. We treat the employee experience the way great product teams treat user experience: with rigor, ownership, and a relentless focus on removing friction.

The People Business Partner is a critical node in that system. You'll work on both strategy and execution - partnering with people managers to build high-performing teams, owning the infrastructure that makes our people operations reliable and scalable, and continuously improving the systems that shape how KOHOnians experience work. You’ll work cross-functionally with Talent and Coaching to achieve our goals.

This is not a support role. It's a builder role for someone who thinks in systems, operates with a high degree of autonomy, and holds themselves accountable to outcomes.

We are open to hiring at the intermediate or senior level. This role reports to the Director, People and Culture.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN


STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP

 * Serve as a trusted advisor to people managers across org design, performance, succession, and leadership effectiveness

 * Bring a data-informed perspective to talent decisions - identifying risks early and shaping proactive responses before they become reactive ones

 * Contribute to KOHO's 2026 People Enablement strategy, with a particular lens on compensation, performance and the full employee lifecycle


PEOPLE OPERATIONS

 * Support the full employee journey: from onboarding through transitions, with consistency and care at every stage

 * Proactively identify opportunities to streamline People Ops workflows, leveraging AI and automation to reduce manual overhead

 * Ensure BambooHR data accuracy and integrity - you're the steward of the systems people rely on


COMPLIANCE

 * Stay current on legislation, trends, and best practices impacting compensation, benefits, immigration, and people operations in Canada and the US

 * Translate regulatory changes into clear internal guidance, without bureaucratic overhead


REQUIREMENTS:

 * You have 5+ years of experience in People Business Partnering preferably with both Canada and the US markets

 * You operate comfortably as a strategic owner, accountable for results

 * Demonstrated analytical abilities, attention to detail and the ability to successfully manage multiple competing tasks and priorities

 * Exceptional knowledge and understanding of HR policies and processes

 * Comfort with AI, we are AI Native at KOHO



The budgeted salary range for this role, based on job level:

 * Intermediate Level: $110,000 - $130,000 CAD / year.

 * Senior Level: $130,000 - $160,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.




DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS




À PROPOS DU POSTE

KOHO est en pleine transformation : nous passons d’une fonction RH traditionnelle à un modèle moderne de People Enablement. Nous abordons l’expérience employé comme les meilleures équipes produit abordent l’expérience utilisateur : avec rigueur, sens des responsabilités et une obsession pour éliminer les irritants.

Le ou la Partenaire d’affaires principal(e), Ressources humaines joue un rôle clé dans cette évolution. Vous travaillerez autant sur la stratégie que sur l’exécution — en accompagnant les gestionnaires dans la création d’équipes performantes, en assurant la fiabilité et l’évolutivité de nos opérations RH, et en améliorant continuellement les systèmes qui façonnent l’expérience de travail chez KOHO. Vous collaborerez étroitement avec les équipes Talent et Coaching afin d’atteindre nos objectifs communs.

Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle de soutien administratif. C’est un rôle de bâtisseur pour une personne qui pense en systèmes, qui fonctionne avec un haut niveau d’autonomie et qui est responsable des résultats.

Ce poste relève du Directeur, Personnes et Culture.




CE QUE VOUS PRENDREZ EN CHARGE


PARTENARIAT STRATÉGIQUE

 * Agir à titre de partenaire de confiance auprès des gestionnaires en matière de structure organisationnelle, gestion de la performance, planification de la relève et efficacité du leadership

 * Apporter une perspective basée sur les données aux décisions liées aux talents, en identifiant les risques tôt et en proposant des solutions proactives avant qu’ils ne deviennent des enjeux réactifs

 * Contribuer à la stratégie 2026 de People Enablement chez KOHO, notamment en matière de rémunération, de performance et d’expérience employé globale


OPÉRATIONS RH

 * Soutenir l’ensemble du parcours employé : de l’intégration jusqu’aux transitions, avec cohérence, efficacité et empathie

 * Identifier de façon proactive des occasions d’optimiser les processus RH, notamment par l’utilisation de l’IA et de l’automatisation afin de réduire les tâches manuelles

 * Assurer l’exactitude et l’intégrité des données dans BambooHR — vous serez responsable des systèmes sur lesquels les employés comptent au quotidien


CONFORMITÉ

 * Maintenir une connaissance à jour des lois, tendances et meilleures pratiques liées à la rémunération, aux avantages sociaux, à l’immigration et aux opérations RH au Canada et aux États-Unis

 * Traduire les changements réglementaires en directives internes claires et simples, sans lourdeur bureaucratique




EXIGENCES

 * Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience en partenariat d’affaires RH, idéalement dans les marchés canadien et américain

 * Capacité à agir comme propriétaire stratégique, avec une forte responsabilisation face aux résultats

 * Excellentes aptitudes analytiques, souci du détail et capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités simultanément

 * Solide compréhension des politiques et processus RH

 * Aisance avec l’intelligence artificielle — chez KOHO, nous sommes une organisation AI Native




RÉMUNÉRATION

L’échelle salariale prévue pour ce poste est de 110 000 $ à 140 000 $ CAD par année.

Chez KOHO, nous croyons en la transparence salariale pour tous les candidats. La rémunération est établie selon plusieurs facteurs, incluant notamment les données de marché au Canada, l’évaluation des compétences, l’expérience professionnelle globale et l’équité interne avec les autres membres de l’équipe KOHO.

KOHO is for builders.



If you’re energized by challenge, motivated by mission, and want to be part of a team that punches above its weight - we want to hear from you.

 

The KOHO culture is one of collaboration, creativity, and diverse perspectives. We are committed to building and fostering an inclusive, accessible environment for everyone. ABOUT THE ROLE

KOHO is looking for a Senior Manager, Financial Risk Strategy & Analytics to lead key strategy and analytics initiatives within our financial risk management function. Bridging the gap between deep technical analysis and strategic leadership, you will own complex models and forecasts while mentoring a team of analysts. Working closely with Finance, Product, and Data teams, you will turn complex data into actionable insights, ensuring our growth is resilient and compliant while safeguarding KOHO’s portfolio.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


TEAM LEADERSHIP & MENTORSHIP

 * Manage and mentor a team of individual contributors across Financial Risk domains.

 * Foster a culture of rigorous analysis, ownership, and continuous improvement.




FINANCIAL RISK ANALYTICS & FORECASTING

 * Forecasting & Provisioning: Lead the development, execution, and enhancement of short- and long-term delinquency and loss forecasting models. Oversee Expected Credit Loss (ECL) calculations and the monthly provisioning process in strict accordance with IFRS 9 standards.

 * Stress Testing: Execute and review stress tests for financial risks to ensure KOHO maintains adequate liquidity and capital buffers in line with regulatory requirements and internal risk appetite. Design, execute, and refine comprehensive stress testing scenarios to assess portfolio resilience under adverse macroeconomic conditions.

 * Market & Liquidity Risk: Oversee monitoring and reporting frameworks for non-credit financial risks, including interest rate, market, and liquidity risk. Perform a second line of defense role in understanding and challenging the data, models, and assumptions used in risk assessments.

 * Portfolio Monitoring: Oversee portfolio health monitoring, identifying emerging trends and risks through rigorous analysis of internal performance data and external indicators. Identify opportunities for automated anomaly detection.

 * Impact Assessment: Partner with Product and Marketing to assess the credit risk impact of new initiatives, quantifying potential effects on delinquency, losses, and provisions before launch.

 * Model Risk Management: Performs second line oversight of models used in decisions impacting financial risk.




CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION & INSIGHT GENERATION

 * Reporting & Insights: Produce and present high-quality reporting for senior leadership, translating complex analytical results into clear, strategic recommendations.

 * Data Strategy: Collaborate with Data Analytics and Data Science to enhance data pipelines and infrastructure, identifying new data sources, and ensuring the integrity and availability of risk data. Act as a steward for critical risk data.

 * Strategic Partnership: Work closely with Finance on capital planning and economic forecasting, and with Product to optimize credit strategies based on risk-adjusted returns.




WHO YOU ARE

Experience & Education

 * 6-8 years of experience in financial risk management, with deep hands-on experience in retail credit risk analytics, loss forecasting, and treasury risk.

 * Leadership: Proven experience leading analytical workstreams and managing or mentoring individual contributors.

 * Education: A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Engineering) or equivalent practical experience.




SKILLS & COMPETENCIES

 * Technical Expertise: Strong proficiency in SQL, Python, or SAS for data manipulation and modeling. Deep understanding of IFRS 9 standards, ECL methodologies, and stress testing frameworks.

 * Analytical Rigor: Exceptional ability to independently build complex models, perform root cause analysis, and ensure high standards of quality across the team's output.

 * Risk Knowledge: Familiarity with market and liquidity risk concepts, ALM (Asset Liability Management), and stress testing frameworks.

 * Communication: Strong ability to tell a story with data, clearly explaining technical risk concepts and their business implications to non-technical stakeholders and senior executive leadership.

 * Builder Mindset: You are comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where you often need to build tools, processes, and frameworks from scratch.




KOHO IS FOR BUILDERS

If you’re energized by challenge, motivated by mission, and want to be part of a team that punches above its weight, we want to hear from you. The KOHO culture is one of collaboration, creativity, and diverse perspectives. We are committed to building and fostering an inclusive, accessible environment for everyone.

Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.




DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS




À PROPOS DU POSTE

KOHO est à la recherche d'un Gestionnaire principal, Stratégie et analyse des risques financiers pour diriger des initiatives clés au sein de notre fonction de gestion des risques. En faisant le pont entre l'analyse technique approfondie et le leadership stratégique, vous serez responsable de modèles et de prévisions complexes tout en encadrant une équipe d'analystes. En collaboration étroite avec les équipes des finances, des produits et des données, vous transformerez des données complexes en informations exploitables, garantissant ainsi que notre croissance est résiliente et conforme, tout en protégeant le portefeuille de KOHO.




CE QUE VOUS FEREZ


LEADERSHIP D'ÉQUIPE ET MENTORAT

 * Gérer et encadrer une équipe de contributeurs individuels dans les différents domaines du risque financier.

 * Favoriser une culture d'analyse rigoureuse, de responsabilisation et d'amélioration continue.





ANALYSE ET PRÉVISIONS DES RISQUES FINANCIERS

 * Prévisions et provisions : Diriger l'élaboration, l'exécution et l'amélioration des modèles de prévision des impayés et des pertes à court et à long terme. Superviser les calculs des pertes de crédit attendues (PCA/ECL) et le processus de provisionnement mensuel en stricte conformité avec les normes IFRS 9.

 * Tests de résistance (Stress Testing) : Exécuter et réviser les tests de résistance pour les risques financiers afin de s'assurer que KOHO maintient des liquidités et des réserves de capital adéquates, conformément aux exigences réglementaires et à l'appétit pour le risque interne. Concevoir et affiner des scénarios complets pour évaluer la résilience du portefeuille dans des conditions macroéconomiques défavorables.

ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.




ABOUT THE ROLE

KOHO is looking for a Director, Financial Risk to lead the strategy and analytics efforts within our financial risk management function. In this pivotal role, you will oversee both Credit Risk and Non-Credit Financial Risk (including Market and Liquidity Risk), managing a team of people managers and experts to safeguard KOHO’s financial health while enabling sustainable growth.

Working closely with Product, Finance, Technology, and Data teams, you will lead a team of financial risk subject matter experts in the development and implementation of analytical frameworks that drive our risk decisions and ensure regulatory compliance. In addition to being the financial risk SME in the development of risk and valuation models, you will have end-to-end ownership for risk appetite metrics and loss forecasting, IFRS 9 provisioning, and portfolio monitoring. You will also provide "effective challenge" and decision governance across the organization.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


LEAD & DEVELOP THE TEAM

 * Manage and mentor a high-performing team of people managers and individual contributors across all Financial Risk domains.

 * Foster a culture of rigorous analysis, ownership, and continuous improvement.


FINANCIAL RISK GOVERNANCE & OVERSIGHT

 * Decision Governance: Establish and maintain robust decision governance frameworks for key business decisions with Financial Risk impact, ensuring that they align with KOHO’s risk appetite.

 * Effective Challenge: Provide "effective challenge" on decisions impacting financial risk, such as model development and performance monitoring activities by Tech/Data Science, financial risk-related inputs to stress testing provided by first-line teams, or new product or marketing initiatives proposed by Product.

 * Risk Appetite: Oversee and recommend the frameworks for assessing and measuring our financial risk appetite, lead the financial risk appetite approval process by senior leadership and the board, and lead the development and monitoring of the risk appetite metrics.

 * Policy: Lead governance for financial risk policies including credit policy, across product portfolios, monitor for behavior trends and shifts, and use monitoring results to recommend and implement immediate changes, such as tightening credit limits.

 * Model Risk Management: Leads second line oversight of models used in decisions impacting financial risk.


FINANCIAL RISK STRATEGY & ANALYTICS

 * Forecasting & Provisioning: Oversee short- and long-term delinquency and loss forecasting. Lead the calculation of Expected Credit Loss (ECL), stress testing, and provisioning in strict accordance with IFRS 9 standards.

 * Market & Liquidity Risk: Collaborate with Finance and Treasury teams in the development and execution of forecasting frameworks for market and liquidity risk. Establish monitoring and reporting for Financial Risks.

 * Stress Testing: Lead the stress testing process for financial risk, including the methodology and scenario selection process. Provide effective challenge to first line teams that create the financial risk-related inputs to stress testing, including to Finance teams on liquidity and market risk-related methodologies and forecasts..

 * Portfolio Monitoring: Drive portfolio risk monitoring, reporting, and insight generation to identify trends, risks, and opportunities early. Identify and drive opportunities for automated anomaly detection leveraging state-of-the-art tools and techniques.

 * Data Stewardship: Act as the primary steward for Financial Risk data. This includes identification and/or definition of new data sources/elements for risk-related decision making; identification/documentation of critical data elements; working with the Data and Technology teams in the documentation of all associated metadata (including data lineage); and ensuring data quality, integrity, and availability for decision-making.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 * Partner closely with Finance on capital planning, provisioning, and forecasting. Collaborate with Finance in the design, execution, and oversight of comprehensive stress testing programs for financial risks to ensure KOHO’s readiness in the face of adverse events.

 * Collaborate with Product Management to embed risk insights into new product development and feature optimization.

 * Collaborate with Marketing to assess the risk impact of marketing initiatives.

 * Work with Technology, Data Analytics, and Data Science to enhance risk infrastructure, data pipelines, models, and modeling capabilities.


WHO YOU ARE


EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION

 * 10+ years of experience in financial risk management, with significant exposure to retail credit risk and/or treasury/financial risk management.

 * Leadership: Proven experience managing people managers and leading high-performing analytical teams.

 * Education: A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Engineering) or equivalent practical experience.


SKILLS & COMPETENCIES

 * Technical Expertise: Deep understanding of IFRS 9 standards, ECL methodologies, and stress testing frameworks. Familiarity with market and liquidity risk principles.

 * Analytical Mindset: Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable strategic insights.

 * Communication: Strong ability to communicate complex risk concepts to non-technical stakeholders and senior executive leadership.

 * Collaboration: A "builder" mindset—you thrive in cross-functional environments and can effectively influence peers in Product, Finance, and Tech.



The budgeted salary range for this role is $180,000-$240,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.




DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

KOHO est à la recherche d’un·e Directeur·trice, Risque financier, pour piloter la stratégie et les analyses au sein de notre fonction de gestion du risque financier. Dans ce rôle clé, tu vas superviser à la fois le risque de crédit et le risque financier hors crédit (incluant le risque de marché et de liquidité). Tu vas diriger une équipe de gestionnaires et d’expert·es pour garder la santé financière de KOHO solide, tout en soutenant une croissance durable.

CE QUE TU FERAS


VOICI À QUOI VA RESSEMBLER TON QUOTIDIEN.

Diriger et développer l’équipe

 * Gouvernance décisionnelle : Mettre en place et maintenir des cadres de gouvernance décisionnelle robustes pour les décisions d’affaires qui ont un impact sur le risque financier, en veillant à ce qu’elles soient alignées sur l’appétit pour le risque de KOHO.

 * Prévisions et provisionnement : Superviser les prévisions de défaut et de pertes à court et à long terme. Diriger le calcul de la Perte de crédit attendue (ECL), les tests de résistance et le provisionnement, en stricte conformité avec la norme IFRS 9.

 * Risque de marché et de liquidité : Collaborer avec les équipes Finance et Trésorerie pour développer et exécuter des cadres de prévision du risque de marché et de liquidité. Mettre en place le suivi et la production de rapports sur les risques financiers.

 * Tests de résistance : Diriger le processus de tests de résistance pour le risque financier, y compris la méthodologie et la sélection des scénarios. Offrir un challenge constructif aux équipes de première ligne qui créent les intrants liés au risque financier pour ces tests. Par exemple, challenger les équipes Finance sur les méthodologies et les prévisions liées au risque de liquidité et au risque de marché.

Identifier et mener des initiatives d’automatisation de la détection d’anomalies en s’appuyant sur des outils et techniques de pointe.

jobs.description_text:
COME BUILD A BETTER FINANCIAL FUTURE FOR ALL CANADIANS

THE HONEST VERSION OF THIS JOB

Neo is about to significantly increase its marketing spend. The question is whether the analytical infrastructure exists to make sure that investment is working. Right now, it doesn't fully.

Attribution is fragmented. Channel performance is hard to compare cleanly. The insights that should be driving budget allocation decisions exist in pieces across different people and systems, and they're not consistently making it to the people who need them. This role changes that.

This is not a dashboard job. It's a job for someone who is genuinely fascinated by what the data says and won't rest until that understanding shapes how the business moves. The work you do here will directly inform how tens of millions of dollars get spent and where Neo grows fastest. That's the scope.

 
 


WHAT YOU'RE WALKING INTO

The marketing analytics function doesn't exist in a consolidated form yet. You're building it. You'll report to the CMO and work closely with the marketing team that is growing and increasing its spend meaningfully.

The data infrastructure is real. Neo runs on Snowflake and has the raw material to answer hard questions. What's missing is the person who knows which questions to ask and can turn the answers into decisions.

You won't manage a team. What you will do is set the analytical direction for how an entire marketing org measures its work, allocates its budget, and decides what to do next. The leverage is significant.

 
 


WHAT THIS JOB ACTUALLY REQUIRES

You're obsessed with the outcome, not the output. The wrong version of this role produces clean reports that nobody acts on. The right version produces insights that change what the team does next week. You're the right version. You follow the data until it tells you something useful, and then you make sure it lands.

You ask the question nobody thought to ask. Any analyst can answer the question in front of them. The people who create real value are the ones who come to a meeting with the question the team didn't know it had. That's the habit we're looking for.

You can communicate findings to people who don't live in the data. The CMO and marketing leads need to understand what you're telling them well enough to act on it. That requires the ability to translate analytical work into clear, direct business language without losing the nuance that makes it true.



You've done this in a consumer context. You understand acquisition costs, channel efficiency, attribution complexity, and the messiness of real marketing data. B2C or high-growth tech backgrounds translate well here. Consulting pedigrees without hands-on data work do not.

 


WHAT WE'RE NOT LOOKING FOR

Someone who measures success by the quality of their analysis rather than the quality of the decisions it drives. Accuracy is necessary. It's not sufficient.

Someone who waits to be asked. If you need someone to hand you a question before you start digging, the impact ceiling is low. We want someone who treats the data as a source of problems worth finding, not a system to query on demand.

Someone without consumer or B2C exposure. The dynamics of marketing measurement in financial services for Canadian consumers are specific. General analytics experience without that context takes too long to become useful.




THE COMPENSATION REALITY

A competitive base salary. A cash-based STIP tied to company performance and individual impact. Meaningful equity with long-term upside tied directly to Neo's growth.

 


THE BASICS

 * 7+ years in marketing analytics or growth analytics with hands-on data work

 * Strong proficiency in SQL; experience with Snowflake is a plus

 * B2C or consumer tech background

 * Demonstrated track record of analytics work that drove measurable business decisions, not just reporting

 * Based in Canada; we work in-person

Neo Financial was founded in 2019 with a straightforward idea: Canadians deserve better. Better products, better rates, better tools for building credit and growing wealth. We've built a team of 700+ people, partnered with 10,000+ retailers, and grown to serve over one million Canadians. We're just getting started.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Derivative Risk Remediation team (DRR) is a small team within Credit Risk Operations (CROPS) responsible for monitoring derivative exposures exceeding $1 billion, which is growing as the business expands its derivative offering. The team identifies and remediates derivative risk across Wealthsimple's retail book — before exposures become losses. We sit at the intersection of live market risk, regulatory compliance, and operational infrastructure, and we hold ourselves to a high bar on all three. The stakes are real: the decisions this team makes have a direct monetary impact on clients and the firm. If you take operational excellence seriously, want to live the Maker-Owner mindset, and have Naive Ambition, you will feel right at home.

 
 


ABOUT THE ROLE

This role is the operational backbone of the Derivative Risk Remediation team. You'll own the day-to-day monitoring, remediation, and reconciliation work that keeps our retail derivatives function running — surfacing risk, executing on it, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks. You'll work closely with the Senior Specialist on cases that require a higher level of judgment, and you'll be a critical part of a small team where consistent coverage isn't optional — it's the whole point.

This isn't a process-execution role. Exposures and account states vary case by case, and no fixed playbook fits every situation. We need someone with sound judgment, solid derivatives knowledge, the analytical instinct to spot issues before they become obvious, and the technical skills to build and maintain the tools the team relies on. Just as important: this role sits at the intersection of several teams, so we're looking for someone who stays objective under pressure and works well across functions.

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 * Monitor dashboards daily to identify derivative risk across the retail book — surfacing concentrations, early assignment events, near-expiry ITM positions, and accounts requiring action, and triaging each case on its merits.

 * Monitor automations during option liquidations and escalate anomalies and failures to Engineering, and ensure changes are implemented to avoid mass failures and stay compliant with policies.

 * Execute option assignment and exercise workflows, account restrictions, position liquidations, and remediation for early assignment, uncovered positions, corporate actions, and ad hoc trade requests from other teams.

 * Review derivative scenarios and assess how each affects margin, buying power, and firm exposure — applying working knowledge of dynamic collateral and strategy re-pairing to size and execute remediation actions.

 * Complete weekly and monthly CIRO audit requirements, documenting findings and controls in JIRA and partnering with the Senior Specialist on any remediation needed.

 * Build and maintain monitoring tools using SQL, Python, and AI tooling — contributing to dashboards and maintaining automation scripts that surface daily risk views and exposure trackers.

 * Contribute data, queries, and visualizations that feed team discussions and Risk Committee reporting.

 * Apply CIRO IDPC margin rules to derivative positions in day-to-day decisions and escalate ambiguous or material cases to the Senior Specialist or Team Lead.

 * Complete ad hoc trades and tasks as assigned by the Senior Specialist or Team Lead.

 
 


SKILLS YOU BRING

 * 1–3 years in derivatives operations, risk, margin operations, or trading support at a CIRO-regulated dealer or equivalent

 * Working knowledge of retail option strategies (verticals, iron condors, butterflies, covered calls, cash-secured puts, naked options) and their basic risk mechanics, plus a working understanding of futures and options on futures

 * Solid grasp of option assignment and exercise mechanics, expiry-day operations, corporate actions, and dividend risk; working knowledge of CIRO IDPC margin rules and of dynamic collateral and strategy re-pairing as they apply to remediation decisions

 * A collaborative mindset — comfortable surfacing risks, contributing to team discussions, and escalating appropriately to the Senior Specialist or leaders

 * Working-to-intermediate SQL (joins, CTEs, basic JSON parsing), Python for automation scripts and basic API integrations, practical use of AI tooling, and working proficiency with BI platforms and Excel

 * CSC, CPH, DFOL, and FLC (or equivalent CIRO new proficiency requirements), or CFA Level 1, are required to register as a supervisor

 
 


NICE TO HAVE

 * OPSC, IDSC, and CCSE certifications

 * CFA or FRM candidacy

 * Experience with futures and futures options

 * Experience with JIRA, Notion, Slack, Oracle DB, ICE, FactSet, Preset, Apache Superset, or similar tools

 
 


WHO YOU ARE

 * A reliable problem solver with sound judgment — able to make calculated, low-error decisions under time pressure where the cost of a mistake is immediate and quantifiable, and where the right action varies case by case

 * Detail-oriented and consistent — you catch things others miss, and you take that responsibility seriously

 * Technically capable and self-sufficient — you're comfortable building and maintaining the tools the team depends on without waiting to be asked

 * Someone who knows when to act and when to escalate — you don't let ambiguity stall you, but you're not too proud to bring in the Senior Specialist when a case warrants it

 * Collaborative by default — you share context early, communicate clearly, and make the team around you more effective




WHY WEALTHSIMPLE?

🌸 Top-tier health benefits and life insurance

📈 Long-term group savings with employer match, through Wealthsimple for Business

🌴 20 vacation days, 4 wellness days, and unlimited sick and mental health days per year

✈️ 90 days away: work outside Canada for up to 90 days per year

👥 Employee resource groups, including Rainbow (2SLGBTQ), Women of WS, and Black at WS

🌎 We are a hybrid team with over 1,500 employees across North America. The people are one of the best parts of working here: you'll collaborate with incredibly talented, curious, and driven teammates who are deeply committed to doing great work.

That means we're always looking for better ways to work — whether that's new tools, AI, or rethinking how we approach a problem. We don't expect you to have all the answers, but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to evolve alongside the products we're building.
